title: The Knight's L
summary: The one piece that goes over the wall instead of around it

steps.title: Two Squares, Then One
steps.text:
Two squares, then one square to the side. That is every knight move there has ever been.

The knight is the only piece that refuses to travel in a straight line. It does not slide along a rank or a file — it hops, from where it stands to where it lands, and touches nothing in between.

Watch it go: {{Nf6}}. Two squares up the board from e4, then one to the right. An **L**, drawn in a single move.

steps.title: Eight Landing Squares
steps.text:
Count them from e4: {{Nd6}}, {{Nf6}}, {{Nc5}}, {{Ng5}}, {{Nc3}}, {{Ng3}}, {{Nd2}}, {{Nf2}}. Eight arrows leaving one square at the same time, and any of the eight is a legal move.

Now stand the same knight in the corner square a1 and count again: two. Six of its L-shapes run off the edge of the board and take their squares with them.

So a knight wants the middle. It is the one piece whose strength you can read off its address.

steps.prompt: Jump the knight anywhere an L will carry it from e4.
steps.hint: Count two squares along a rank or a file, then turn one square to the side. Every direction works.

steps.title: Never the Same Color Twice
steps.text:
The square e4 is light. Every one of the eight squares the knight just reached is dark.

That holds everywhere on the board. A knight changes the color under its feet with every single hop, and it has no say in the matter.

Which gives you a free piece of arithmetic: anything standing on a light square is out of reach of a knight on a light square. Out of reach this move, at least. Next move it is the other way around.

steps.title: Over the Wall
steps.text:
Every game begins in a traffic jam. The bishops, the rooks and the queen are sealed in behind their own pawns, and each of them has to wait for a pawn to step out of the road.

The knights do not wait. {{Nf3}} clears the pawn line on move one, and the pawn on f2 never so much as feels a draft.

That is why the knights are so often the first pieces to leave the back rank.

> Everyone else needs a door. The knight goes over the wall.

steps.prompt: Your knight is attacked, so leave the square and take the black pawn that nothing is guarding.
steps.hint: A knight ignores whatever stands in the way, so look past the pawn wall — then ask which pawn beyond it has a second pawn ready to take back.
